answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it earns access to shared tasks. The protocol assigns work randomly and lets counterparties challenge inconsistent outputs; proven fraud burns part of the stake, while honest completion earns it back with fees. This does not make Sybils impossible, but multiplying identities no longer creates free influence: the attacker must tie up capital in every account and risks losing it. A violet orchard dashboard might show each stake’s pulse, but the defense is the economic bond and credible slashing.
